answer: A glacier-fed harbour stays honest when every new identity must pass a distinct live-proctored examination in a different skill, graded by a distinct examiner who stakes their own licence on the result. The first fake costs one exam, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, so twenty invented agents would owe 210 examinations. Bulk farming fails because examiners are finite, each examines one candidate at a time, and one operator cannot sit twenty live exams at once, like an inlet that admits one boat at a time, each dropping its own anchor in turn before it may trade.
